Application 9.4.1 requires DB 9.11.1 (minimum and target), upgraded from 9.11.0. Text-only migration seeds 23 language keys, fills missing/blank translations and exact English fallbacks in non-English locales, preserving other authored copy. At each article UI permission's first creation, users/guests keep Details and lose Images, Attachments, Related rows, Task progress and Edit/Edit language versions/Delete until granted; later grants/revocations persist. Anonymous visitors receive their guest group's UI grants. Home keeps its full site name, phone layout and sharp 128 px site icons. Home article buttons are server-side, configured through the administrator API; Home rendering follows in a later release.

Application 9.4.2 requires DB 9.11.2 (minimum and target), upgraded from 9.11.1. Text-only migration seeds article-view explanations and group field-setting warnings in Finnish, English, Chinese and Cantonese, filling only missing/blank translations; no right is granted or removed. Missing article-view rights remove clickable styling and explain attempted openings; group view settings warn and live updates stop retrying after 401/403. Administrators choose Home article buttons below text or as top-row pills; the open menu keeps its button. Optional operator Home at / stays off until data/storage/site_root/index.html exists and the Home switch is on; login_to_browse still decides access. Pages, favicon and shared-link previews use site identity and Home slogan fallbacks. Hidden source columns hide generated name filters. Lazy modules preload from /frontend/dist/. Runner images require its configured upload directory, identical to the web server's; no directory refuses images while text works. Readiness requires ChatGPT subscription sign-in; API-key logins remain unavailable. Image-first panels gain rounded corners and responsive spacing; the photo rounds after scrolling. Product view names survive startup; the development layout lock appears only in Cards and Article.

Application 9.4.3 keeps DB 9.11.2 unchanged (minimum and target); upgrading from 9.4.2 needs no database step, migration or database release record. Opening an article from cards styles newly bound surfaces without repainting every card, preserving appearance, previews and themes. Development desktop measurements on 60 rows: CSS writes 52,307 to 866, longest main-thread task about 290 ms to 120 ms, click to visible article about 470 ms to 250 ms; these are not production timing guarantees. Large datasets gain most: fintravel.fi's reported 6.5-second freeze came from repaint work growing with the square of visible cards. Administrators' Workline observatory has one desktop content scrollbar instead of two; phone/tablet scrolling at 900 px and below is unchanged. A shared article-presentation contract has no visible effect or new presentation; operators can optionally export saved settings and their current resolution as deterministic JSON from a read-only database-copy snapshot that always rolls back, without changing settings or rights. Developer tooling accepts explicit Claude worker effort; a browser-test locator was corrected.

Application 9.5.0 upgrades database 9.11.2 to 9.12.0 on first start; minimum and target are 9.12.0. The 21 migrations preserve and materialize article settings and audiences in ordered per-presentation bundles with an atomic combined-editor save, add per-image-use card presentation and focal points, extend filter bar preferences, associate object translations with read-rights ownership, add the three-line table-cell default (administrator range 1–30), seed reviewed interface wording while preserving site edits, make first-run suggestions read-only, add category heading order and record the database release last. New opener activation, Page layout and the image-presentation editor remain later work. Filter sections share stable layout, order and visibility choices; category matching is explained; administrators can save dataset default views; readable datasets offer text search independently of AI rights; integer-ID matches lead results. Home stays first and reachable, uses the matching side menu and offers optional Serif story text. Cards, tiles and articles share safe localized record names; rich-text links retain safe destinations and article arrows are centred. Image sourcing prefers decodable formats, retaining AVIF at lower priority. Read boundaries cover object names, linked labels, filter values, comments and row events; administrator tools, writes, registration and first-run setup are more tightly guarded. Every first-administrator submission requires the server-log setup code. Maintenance and payment reads no longer write; language-key retirement remains paused and scans require trustworthy evidence. Notices follow language and account rights. Native restore-check rehearses trusted authenticated packets in temporary databases without stopping the application; stored code still executes as superuser on the live cluster. Go 1.26.9, x/image 0.45.0 and x/text 0.43.0 fix HTTP, WebP and Unicode security issues. PostgreSQL/PostGIS image builds drop expiring pins. Test/tooling improvements and future-feature documentation add no further production capability. Article presentations share one Field settings editor: three projections and opening blocks in a five-column table, preserved group differences and scoped drafts, one atomic revision-checked Save verified by complete readback; phone tables scroll within the page and keep field identity visible.
